analystGuidance.text: For Mauritian cynomolgus macaques, M1 through M7 are ancestral extended MHC haplotypes. Prefer known MCM labels and known recombinant structure before proposing a new MCM haplotype.
analystGuidance.title: MCM labels are extended haplotypes

analystGuidance.text: The M3 reference haplotype is useful for broad organization and locus-neighborhood reasoning. Use it to remember that class II loci such as DP and DQ are not independent in MCM without recombination evidence.
analystGuidance.title: Use M3 as an organization landmark

analystGuidance.text: For Indian-origin rhesus macaques and non-MCM cynomolgus macaques, familiar report labels describe regional haplotype blocks rather than seven whole-MHC ancestral haplotypes. Track A, B, DRB, DQ, and DP evidence independently unless linked evidence supports a larger block.
analystGuidance.title: Use regional block models for complex populations

analystGuidance.text: Short exon amplicons can collapse multiple full-length alleles into one marker label. Full-length or cDNA evidence can expose additional allelic diversity, but subtle private variants should not automatically split a clinically familiar report haplotype.
analystGuidance.title: Separate marker labels from full allele resolution

analystGuidance.text: Use richer internal structure for reasoning, but emit familiar labels such as M1A, M3DR, A008.01, B069.02, and DR01.01 when they fit the evidence so transplantation and infectious disease users can interpret reports.
analystGuidance.title: Preserve digestible curated report labels

analystGuidance.text: Novel MCM whole-MHC haplotypes should be rare. Novel regional haplotypes are more plausible in less studied or more complex populations. Simple founder populations may have constrained haplotypes; sparsely defined populations may need provisional labels.
analystGuidance.title: Tune novelty to population history

markerRules.text: A private or subtle full-length variant at a single marker such as one B22-like genotype should not by itself create a new MCM extended haplotype when the rest of the evidence matches an existing haplotype.

In MCM, DP and DQ lie in the same broad class II neighborhood. Different DP and DQ haplotype assignments require rare recombination evidence, missing marker explanation, or a technical-artifact explanation.
Labels with multiple haplotype names embedded in the marker, such as M1M2M3, represent collapsed assay evidence and must be combined with more informative markers.

Full-length and cDNA data can reveal true allelic variants, but report haplotypes should split only when the variant changes a coherent regional or extended haplotype pattern, not simply because one low-impact allele name differs.
In sparsely characterized or genetically complex macaque populations, coherent new regional haplotype combinations are plausible and should be reported as provisional when evidence supports them.
MHC-AG is near the MHC-A region; AG genotypes should not be emitted as standard report haplotypes yet, but can support or weaken MHC-A regional calls when linked evidence is coherent.

Expected markers can be missing and a haplotype can still be called when the remaining evidence is coherent. Low-read bleed-through should be ignored when dominated by stronger evidence. Homozygous single-haplotype loci are valid calls.

populationProfiles.notes: M1 through M7 span the broad MHC. DP and DQ are in the same broad neighborhood; discordance requires rare recombination, missing data, or technical explanation.
Genome organization is broadly shared with MCM, but non-MCM populations do not have only seven simple ancestral haplotypes. Track DPA, DPB, DQA, and DQB separately unless data support linkage.
Use Mamu A, B, DRB, DQ, and DP regional labels. MHC-E and AG evidence may support nearby calls but is not yet routinely emitted as haplotypes.
Allow overlap between populations and species while keeping population-specific priors explicit; simple founder populations and sparsely defined complex populations need different novelty thresholds.
